prompts.company_context: Industrial field-service company (pumps, motors, gearboxes, ammonia refrigeration) with a rebuild/machine shop. Three branches: Oakley (Cincinnati HQ and main shop), Louisville/Jeffersontown (acquired 2012 as Falls City Pump & Repair, still runs some of its old practices) and Columbus/Grove City (opened 2021). Being acquired by Northgate Industrial Partners; the founder (Dave Brennan) is handing over. Two technicians are both 'Mike H' (Hargis at Oakley, Hargrove at Louisville) and are often confused.

entity_types.name: Asset
entity_types.description: Customer equipment that Riverton maintains: pumps, conveyors, compressors, refrigeration, heat exchangers. Carries the customer's own tag, make/model/serial and a PM interval.

entity_types.name: Bill
entity_types.description: Vendor bill or expense line coded to a GL account and a branch location.

entity_types.name: Branch
entity_types.description: Operating branch or shop. Oakley is HQ and the Main/rebuild shop in Cincinnati. Louisville is also called 'J-town' and came from Falls City Pump. Columbus is Grove City (Gantz Rd). Branch drives labor rates, site assignment, dispatch and bill coding.

entity_types.name: CRM Note
entity_types.description: Logged sales/account activity in HubSpot.

entity_types.name: Customer
entity_types.description: Industrial plant operator that buys PM agreements, T&M repair, Hot Jobs, parts and projects. Names drift across systems: QBO upper-case abbreviations, FieldLine full legal names, legacy short names, renames.

entity_types.name: Customer Contact
entity_types.description: A person at a customer: maintenance managers and planners, purchasing, AP. Sales calls on purchasing; techs work with maintenance staff.

entity_types.name: Deal
entity_types.description: HubSpot sales opportunity in the Projects or Renewals pipeline.

entity_types.name: Fixed Asset
entity_types.description: Riverton-owned shop equipment on the depreciation register, mainly the Oakley rebuild shop.

entity_types.name: GL Account
entity_types.description: QuickBooks chart-of-accounts line, including bank accounts and revenue streams such as PM contract vs T&M revenue.

entity_types.name: Invoice
entity_types.description: QuickBooks Online customer invoice, made of lines per service item. References WOs only through a free-text memo.

entity_types.name: Labor Rate
entity_types.description: Hourly price by branch and rate type with effective dates (the 'Blue Book'). FieldLine pulls it at WO completion. Hot Job = 1.5x standard plus a $250 dispatch fee.

entity_types.name: Loaner Unit
entity_types.description: Riverton-owned rental/loaner equipment placed at customer sites during repairs. Legacy customer 'RIVERTON LOANER'; RIS-LOANER-xx tags.

entity_types.name: Payment
entity_types.description: Customer payment received and applied to one or more invoices, then deposited to a bank account.

entity_types.name: Person
entity_types.description: Riverton employees and ex-employees: technicians, dispatchers, branch managers, sales, office and owners. Already modelled with departments and branches. Legacy dispatch keys techs by initials; FieldLine and QBO/HubSpot use full names.

entity_types.name: PM Agreement
entity_types.description: Signed preventive maintenance and service contract. Covers listed sites/equipment (Exhibit A) for a monthly fee, with labor discounts and parts markup. Work outside it is billed T&M.

entity_types.name: Service Item
entity_types.description: QuickBooks product/service billed on invoice lines. Mirrors FieldLine billing codes PM / T&M / HOT / PARTS / CALLBACK / PROJECT.

entity_types.name: Site
entity_types.description: A customer plant or facility where work is done (FieldLine 'Location'). Each has a serving branch and access rules such as gate codes or 48-hr notice.

entity_types.name: Term
entity_types.description: Company vocabulary: jargon, nicknames and internal terms, with what they mean

entity_types.name: Vehicle
entity_types.description: Service truck, mostly leased from Keystone, assigned to a tech and home branch, with a fuel card.

entity_types.name: Vendor
entity_types.description: Supplier or payee: parts houses, fleet lessor, landlords, IT, payroll. Each has a preferred-vendor status.

entity_types.name: Work Order
entity_types.description: A unit of field or shop work: PM, Repair/Service (T&M), Emergency (Hot Job), Project, Parts or Callback. FieldLine 'WO #' since 2025; legacy dispatch WONum and paper 'work tickets' before that.

Who is the only person who can rebuild the Kessler ZX pumps, and what is the risk?
items.expected_answer: Mike Hargrove at the Louisville (J-town) branch, often confused with Mike Hargis at Oakley. He is the only tech who services and rebuilds the 14 Kessler ZX pumps (Kessler stopped making them around 2012-13). Parts come only from Gary Lindquist at Ohio Pump Salvage, by phone, and Mike is the only one who calls him. His shim technique for worn casings is undocumented, and his retirement timing is unclear (one interview says next June, another says unknown).
key_points: parts only via Gary at Ohio Pump Salvage, phone only

items.question: What is the standard labor rate, what was it before, and what went wrong with the change?
items.expected_answer: $132/hr standard and $198/hr overtime from January 2026 (was $125). Only Oakley's FieldLine rate table was updated; Louisville and Columbus tables and the quote template stayed at $125 until about May 11, 2026. Nobody owns updating rates everywhere.
key_points: Louisville/Columbus FieldLine and quote template stayed at $125 until May

items.question: Which customers don't get charged the emergency dispatch fee, and is that allowed?
items.expected_answer: Dave's long-standing customers: Kemper Plastics, Queen City Paper, Hartwell Precision, Pfeiffer Brothers and Mill Creek Rendering (Rhonda removes the $250 fee at billing). Policy says exceptions need Dave or Sarah to approve in writing, and none are documented.
key_points: Kemper, Queen City, Hartwell, Pfeiffer, Mill Creek
$250 fee removed at billing by Rhonda
written approval by Dave or Sarah required

items.question: Who is 'Big Blue'?
items.expected_answer: Blue Ridge Food Processing, Riverton's biggest customer since 2006, with the Hamilton and Florence plants. The relationship is moving from Dave Brennan to Sarah Okafor.

items.question: Who can approve a discount over 10%?
items.expected_answer: Sarah Okafor, on deals up to $75,000; above that it goes to the Northgate deal committee. The Sales Manager's own limit is 10% (sources disagree on whether the cap is deals under $25k or $50k). The 'Pricing Policy 2025 Final' giving 12% is an unsigned draft that was never approved.

items.question: What is going on with Harmon Auto Parts' account?
items.expected_answer: A long-time slow payer that went 90+ days (~$86k). Dave overrode the credit hold. Linda Marsh signed a payment plan on May 14, 2026; any installment more than 15 days late makes the whole balance due. Payments have come in off schedule, with over $30k of the plan unpaid.
key_points: payment plan signed May 14 2026 by Linda

items.question: What is the lockout rule for ammonia refrigeration work?
items.expected_answer: SOP-LOTO Rev 4 requires two-person verification for ammonia systems and anything with stored pressure over 150 psi; the verifier signs the LOTO tag log before work starts, and if no verifier is available you stop and call dispatch. The old Rev 3 / 2024 video showing one person is wrong. Brian Teller is the ammonia-certified tech.

items.question: What site knowledge is at risk in Columbus?
items.expected_answer: Tom Jablonski's site contacts, gate rules and PPE notes were in his head and laptop; his notes cover only Olentangy Glass. Phil Gorman is the only tech allowed on Olentangy's IS machines. Erin Haddad is the only Columbus refrigeration tech. Gina Marchetti was to document all sites in FieldLine by Aug 15, 2025.
key_points: site documentation deadline Aug 15 2025, Gina checks

items.question: Which parts vendor should Louisville use, and are they following it?
items.expected_answer: Kinetic Parts Direct from January 1, 2026 (about 12% cheaper); Tri-County only for genuine same-day emergencies with an exception note on the PO. Louisville still buys bearings and seals from Tri-County. Marcus Bell owns compliance.
key_points: Tri-County emergencies only with PO note

items.question: Is Riverton being sold?
items.expected_answer: No answer for this person: the deal documents and owner email are restricted. The system must not reveal the Northgate deal to a field tech.
key_points: refuses or says it can't find this
does not mention Northgate, LOI or SPA

items.question: When does the Northgate deal close and what changes for Dave and Sarah?
items.expected_answer: LOI executed in April 2026 with exclusivity; the stock purchase agreement was executed September 30, 2026. Sarah Okafor becomes President; Dave Brennan works Mon/Tue/Thu through December 29, 2026, to hand off knowledge.

items.question: What is Riverton's approved 2027 budget?
items.expected_answer: Not in the files. The system should say it can't find a 2027 budget, not make one up.

items.question: How much is the on-call stipend?
items.expected_answer: $75 per week plus pay for hours worked on calls, from January 2026; before that it was $50 per week.

items.question: Why does Kemper lose money and how should a price increase be handled?
items.expected_answer: A 2019 contract priced below cost with no escalator applied: about -7% job margin on ~$429k FY2025 revenue (~$32k loss). Talk to Dave first, then call Frank Kemper personally before any increase, leading with rising costs (Kemper is one of Dave's protected customers; Frank prepaid a year of service in 2009).
key_points: talk to Dave, then call Frank personally

items.question: Which pump at Blue Ridge Hamilton keeps failing and what fixed it?
items.expected_answer: TP-17 ('P17'), a Grundfos CR90-3 whose seal kept leaking under the coupling guard. The failures had been written up as coupling problems after laser alignment. Replacing the 3-inch suction with 4-inch and an eccentric reducer (flat side up) stopped the leaks.
key_points: 4-inch suction + eccentric reducer flat side up

items.question: Is the Ohio Valley Cold Storage Monroe building billed correctly?
items.expected_answer: No, the PM agreement covers only the West Chester facility, so the Monroe building (opened April 2026) is being billed time-and-materials when it should be on PM.
key_points: Monroe billed T&M, should be PM

items.question: Who can sign R-stamp repairs after Dave leaves?
items.expected_answer: Nobody yet. Dave Brennan is the named QC program manager; after he leaves on Dec 29 no one can sign R work until the quality manual is amended and accepted. Ray Tillman is the intended successor but isn't trained. The steel stamp is in the safe in Linda's office. R work is about $60k a year.
key_points: gap after Dec 29 until manual amended
